pages.text: Jelly is a jellyfish drifting in the ocean. Jellyfish are soft and squishy, and they do not have bones.
Jelly moves with the water. Ocean currents push water like slow rivers, and Jelly drifts along.
Sometimes Jelly pulses his body to move a little. But mostly, currents help Jelly travel far.
Jelly’s tentacles trail behind him. Some jellyfish can sting, so people should look and give space.
Jelly meets tiny fish. Fish dart fast, but Jelly floats slowly, like a soft balloon underwater.
In the deep ocean, it can be darker. Jelly can still drift, even when sunlight is weak.
Jelly’s body is mostly water. That helps him float easily without sinking quickly.
Currents change direction sometimes. Jelly goes wherever the moving water carries him today.
Jelly reminds us: jellyfish drift with currents, are soft with no bones, and we should watch gently from afar.
When night comes, Jelly glows softly in our imagination. The ocean keeps moving, and Jelly keeps drifting.
